title: An elementary obstruction to same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation
description:
A credited self-contained elementary exposition of the source-displayed symmetric ordinary unscaled same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation question. Inputs are nonnegative monotone submodular functions with zero empty-set value and every singleton value one. The conventional meaning of constant is taken to be dimension-independent; Végh’s complete source contribution does not separately print an all-ground-sets quantifier. Both r(S)/alpha <= f(S) <= alpha*r(S) comparisons are retained.

The classical square-root-cardinality input on n elements forces alpha >= n^(1/6). Its exact optimum among all matroids is min over integer 1<=R<=n of max(sqrt(R),sqrt(n)/R), attained by uniform ranks. On m^2 elements the rational cardinality input g(empty)=0 and g(nonempty)=1+(|S|-1)/m forces alpha^2+alpha >= m and alpha >= n^(1/4)/sqrt(2). Sharpness is only for the square-root family. Full quantified proofs and empty, singleton, loop and m=1 boundaries are included.

Credits: DDSSS 2013 Appendix D Lemma D.1 for prior uniform-rank decomposition, with corrected direct difference coefficients; classical concave-cardinality submodularity attributed by Balcan-Harvey to Lovász 1983 (original body unread); GHIM actual root-linear output and query-hard rank-input distinction; Schrijver Section 44.6b, credited there to Helgason, for expanded copied-element representation, distinct from one ordinary rank on original V (Helgason original unread). The input families and their rank-sum structure are classical. Exact one-rank argument and generic-envelope historical attribution are unresolved in the bounded review. No new-function, new-representation, firstness, intellectual-priority, independently evidenced discovery, exhaustive literature or current-worldwide-open-status claim is made. Other unread citation-chain consequences remain unknown.
